tasks.short: Collaborate with rehabilitation specialists on client solutions

steps.what: Review relevant client assessments and each specialist's existing findings
Discuss client goals and reconcile proposed solutions with specialists
Write the therapist's agreed contribution in the rehabilitation plan
Check attribution, goals and limitations and complete the plan contribution

tasks.design: Use native client-context and discipline headings in the rehabilitation-record category {OTHER}. The therapist reads original assessments, collaborates with specialists and writes the actual agreed contribution; only repeated identity and fixed heading entry are removed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Different specialist views need discussion and correct attribution.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing client-linked plan forms can reuse identity and discipline structure.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting goals, uncertain benefit and fitting the solution to the client's life.
tasks.human_edge: Reconcile clinical perspectives with the client's priorities.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated plan structure, with unchanged rehabilitation responsibility.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: existing clinical plan forms can reuse client identity and discipline headings while retaining substantive plan writing and checks.

assumptions: Boundary includes the therapist's actual plan contribution read by the care team. Shares are provisional; specialist labour remains outside the focal denominator with no claimed saving.

Specialists supply their own assessments; the therapist reviews them in s1. s2 produces actual agreed contributions and s3 captures them manually. No free meeting transcript, structured decision feed or automatic clinical recommendation is assumed.

{OTHER} is the rehabilitation clinical record. Test native plan forms first. Only repeated client identity and fixed discipline heading entry, 8% of s3, is removed. All clinical wording, attribution and ordinary ungated saving remain.

This is original documentation within existing care authority, not an automatic order, referral send or formal treatment activation. Any actual separate release or cross-provider send needs its own completed-version check and step.
unknowns: Existing identity/headings already supplied by the form
research_questions: Does native plan context remove genuine repeated entry without losing specialist attribution?

already_counted.description: Source review, specialist discussion, substantive entry and final checks remain.

incremental.description: Therapist checks plan structure after discipline or record changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; 25*0.08=2 repeated-entry hours removed less 0.5 upkeep gives 1.5 net. Cautious case: a cross-provider plan needs bespoke structure, leaving 0.6 hours of client-context reuse and 0.1 net; discussion and clinical wording remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Administer rehabilitation tests and interpret results into plans

steps.what: Administer appropriate vision and functional rehabilitation tests
Enter and check raw responses, test version and testing conditions
Calculate supported test totals and reference scores
Interpret test validity and results against functional needs
Write and check the rehabilitation plan against interpreted needs

tasks.design: Configure licensed, version-specific test arithmetic and native plan headings in the rehabilitation-record category {OTHER}. The therapist still administers tests, enters and verifies responses, checks calculated scores and chooses and records the rehabilitation plan; no automated interpretation or treatment allocation is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scoring can be repetitive, but invalid testing conditions can make the result clinically misleading.
tasks.enabler_now: Native scoring rules can remove arithmetic for supported tests after verified capture.
tasks.still_hard: Test validity, visual fatigue, functional context and choosing practical goals.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a numerical score misrepresents the client's abilities.
tasks.altitude: Less scoring arithmetic and plan layout, with unchanged clinical decisions.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: version-specific test arithmetic can be configured deterministically while clinical validity and rehabilitation planning remain professional judgement.

assumptions: Boundary spans test administration, raw entry, scoring, interpretation and the original plan. Shares are hypotheses, not measured.

The therapist produces responses in s1 and captures client/test identifier, test version, raw responses, units and conditions in s2. Approved test owners supply scoring rules and applicable reference tables. No free structured test feed is assumed; missing responses or unsupported versions are scored manually within retained s4-s5 time.

Test native licensed scoring first. s3 is actual human arithmetic today, not existing machine runtime. Retained s4 includes checking raw responses against scores and manual repair. s5 loses only fixed goal/plan heading layout, 10%; substantive plan, clinical checks and ordinary ungated save remain.

Original plan creation is not an order release or referral send. Add actual formal treatment commitments or cross-provider communications separately if required. Shared client context upkeep with collaboration task must be owned once.
unknowns: Licensed scoring availability and supported versions
research_questions: Can native scoring reproduce known test cases while preserving test-version and condition checks?

already_counted.description: Raw capture, validity checking, manual score repair and plan decisions remain.

incremental.description: Therapist validates scoring and reference tables after test-version changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; 10 arithmetic hours plus 15*0.10=1.5 layout hours removed less 1 upkeep gives 10.5 net. Cautious case: an uncommon test lacks supported norms, leaving 2.2 hours of simple supported totals and 0.3 plan-layout hours removed, or 1.5 net; interpretation and repair remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Train clients to read or write Braille

steps.what: Select and prepare suitable Braille practice materials
Teach Braille reading or writing and guide tactile practice
Assess reading or writing errors and adapt the next practice
outputs: assessed Braille progress and next focus

steps.what: Record observed progress and next focus in the existing therapy note
inputs: assessed Braille progress and next focus

tasks.design: Configure goal and Braille-code bookmarks in the existing {DOCS} exercise library to remove repeated browsing. Keep material suitability checks, tactile teaching, error assessment and the actual progress note in the rehabilitation-record category {OTHER} fully human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Exercises must fit the client's tactile skill, code knowledge and fatigue.
tasks.enabler_now: Native library bookmarks shorten retrieval of existing verified exercises.
tasks.still_hard: Tactile discrimination, confidence and adapting practice without frustration.
tasks.human_edge: Notice how the client explores a cell and tailor feedback immediately.
tasks.altitude: A little less exercise browsing, with the same teaching relationship.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: existing Braille exercise libraries can be indexed for retrieval; tactile instruction and learner assessment remain human.

assumptions: Boundary is a therapy session including the existing short progress note used to choose the next session's focus. Verify actual note use and provisional shares; no new unused teaching log is introduced.

The therapist supplies goals from the current plan; approved exercises already carry code/level identifiers. s1 checks suitability manually and prepares physical materials; missing or unclassified exercises are found manually within retained s1.

Test native {DOCS} bookmarks first. Only repeated browsing, 10% of s1, is removed; selection and physical preparation stay. No automatic text-to-Braille conversion, embossing service or new metadata capture is assumed.

The therapist produces progress observations in s2-s3 and enters the original note in s4. Native note fields do not remove its observed content entry; its ordinary save remains fully retained without a self-gate. No material send or new order is hidden.
unknowns: Actual exercise metadata and browsing effort
research_questions: Can native code/level bookmarks remove browsing without mismatching the client's Braille code?

already_counted.description: Exercise suitability, preparation, teaching, assessment and original note entry remain.

incremental.description: Therapist checks exercise bookmarks after library changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; 15*0.10=1.5 browsing hours removed less 0.5 upkeep gives 1 net. Cautious case: a different Braille code requires manual exercise comparison, leaving 0.6 hours of known-library navigation removed and 0.1 net; tactile work and notes remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Small native record and retrieval changes plus supported scoring reduce clerical work; rehabilitation goals and client training stay with the therapist.
role.ambitious_version: No automatic rehabilitation allocation or broader clinical authority is proposed.
